title: Time Complexity of Binary Search
statement: What is the worst-case and best-case time complexity of searching an element in a sorted array of size N using Binary Search?

options.text: Worst: O(log N), Best: O(log N)
Worst: O(N log N), Best: O(1)

explanation: Binary search divides the search space in half at each step leading to O(log N) worst-case time complexity. If the middle element is the target on the first comparison, the best-case time complexity is O(1).

title: Properties of Inorder Traversal in BST
statement: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which tree traversal yields the nodes in strictly non-decreasing (sorted) order?
explanation: Inorder traversal visits Left Subtree -> Root -> Right Subtree. Since BST guarantees Left < Root < Right, inorder traversal always prints node values in strictly sorted ascending order.

title: Shortest Path Algorithm with Non-Negative Weights
statement: Which graph algorithm is most optimal for finding the single-source shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights using a Min-Heap/Priority Queue?

options.text: Dijkstra's Algorithm — O((V + E) log V)

explanation: Dijkstra's algorithm with a Min-Heap efficiently finds the single-source shortest path in O((V + E) log V) for graphs with non-negative edge weights.

title: 0/1 Knapsack State Space and Complexity
statement: What is the time and auxiliary space complexity of the standard bottom-up Dynamic Programming solution for the 0/1 Knapsack Problem with N items and capacity W?

options.text: Time: O(N * W), Space: O(W) or O(N * W)
Time: O(N log W), Space: O(1)

explanation: 0/1 Knapsack DP constructs a 2D table dp[N+1][W+1] (or 1D array dp[W+1] using space optimization), leading to pseudo-polynomial time complexity of O(N * W) and space O(W).

title: Average vs Worst Case Hash Table Search
statement: What are the average-case and worst-case time complexities of searching an element in a Hash Table with chaining collisions?
explanation: Assuming a uniform hash function, average lookup is O(1). In the worst case (all keys hash to the exact same bucket), the chain degrades to a linked list with O(N) search.
